summary: S2 (our 74-85) adapts the Galopoula invasion (ch 121-136, vol 15-16) and B-Rank Wars Rounds 5-6 plus Hyuse's enlistment (ch 137-160, vol 16-18); S3 (our 86-99) adapts Round 7 vs Azuma/Kageura/Suzunari-1 (ch 160-175, vol 18-20), the Hyuse-rumour interlude (176-183) and the Round 8 final vs Ninomiya/Yuba/Ikoma (184-196 p.4, vol 21-22). Every episode is mapped at page level by the World Trigger fandom wiki (its chapter pages' reverse 'Episode' field is consistent for all of ch 118-198), mirrored verbatim by worldtriggerwiki.com and animefillerguide; 24 of 26 anchors are additionally pinned by lineage-independent sources (MAL manga-reader posts with exact chapters at eps 74/85/86/89/96, CBR, ANN, Sportskeeda/WDTALO at ep 99, and chapter-final cliffhangers such as Kakizaki's point-blank shot = last panel of ch 142). Structural surprise: the S2 premiere re-adapts what the S1 finale had pulled forward (ch 120 tail, 121 p.1-11, 123 p.9-19, 124) and skips ch 122 entirely, and the S1 finale had grafted three pages of ch 136; the stored ep 73 chapters_adapted is garbled and is repaired here. Sixteen episodes end mid-chapter, so 16 continue points are supplied; the series ends at ch 196 p.4, which means the entry's continue_from_chapter=197 is one chapter late (flagged). No type corrections; all 26 rows are canon and cumulative numbering 74-99 is confirmed by Wikipedia, fandom and worldtriggerwiki.

anchors.note: S2 premiere (S2E1). Re-adapts material S1 ep 73 had pulled forward: ch 120 tail, 121 p.1-11, 123 p.9-19 and all of 124, then advances through 125 (Galopoula raid on HQ). Ch 122 (Ai Kitora 5) is NOT in this episode - it was adapted only in ep 73. START=121: p.1-11 is the head of the chapter (the remainder was adapted in eps 72-73), so 121 is where an S2 reader begins; the 120 tail is 3 pages. Independent: MAL poster 'half chapter 121 and 123 and full chapter 124 125' + 'they decided to redo the parts they covered in ep 73'; CBR 'premiere starts from Chapter 121'.

S2E2. Border's counterattack on Galopoula; top attackers vs Gatlin/Ratarykov begins. Ends mid-129 (p.1-9). Fandom (page-level) + worldtriggerwiki + afg agree exactly; MAL thread only corroborates arc content (Jin's side effect, Yomi's trion-soldier controller), no end-pinning independent check - hence medium.

S2E3. Nasu defeats Wen So (ch 130), Miwa/Yosuke/Jin defeat Koskero (ch 131), Reghindetz's feint and the Gatlin/Rata fight still unresolved at episode end (Gatlin falls in ch 133, next ep) - MAL thread describes exactly this state ('two enemies already captured', arc to conclude next episode). START=130 by majority rule (129 p.10-19 is a 10-page tail of a 66-page episode).

S2E4. Gatlin/Rata defeated (133), Yotaro fake-death and Hyuse's bet with Jin (134-135, chapter titles 'Yotaro Rindo 2'/'Hyuse'), Galopoula retreats and Round 5 is about to begin (136). MAL thread: fake-death scheme, retreat, 'squad preparing for B-Rank Wars resumption' = 136. Ends mid-136: p.1-12 plus the final page 19; p.13-18 deferred to ep 78.

S2E5. Round 5 (Tamakoma-2 vs Katori vs Kakizaki) begins, ch 137 'Katori Squad'; spider-wire strategy (138); ends with Chika switching to Ibis and firing at the building (139 p.18) - MAL thread: 'ending with Chika's strategic weapon switch'. Only p.19 of 139 remains for ep 79. START=137 (136 p.12-19 is an 8-page tail).

S2E6. Chika's bombardment (140-141), Kakizaki backstory (142 'Kuniharu Kakizaki'); cliffhanger = Kakizaki shoots Yuma point-blank, which is the final panel of ch 142 (fandom long summary) and the cliffhanger every MAL poster discusses. Exact end pinned independently. Aired 2021-02-21 after a one-week earthquake delay (Wikipedia).

S2E7. Round 5 conclusion: Osamu takes two points with wires (143), Katori/Somei flashback (144 'Yoko Katori'), Yuma finishes the wire-restrained Katori with Scorpion = last page of ch 145. MAL thread describes exactly these beats and the round ending. Clean chapter end.

S2E8. Post-match review (146), Hyuse states he will join Tamakoma-2 if taken to Aftokrator (147 'Hyuse 2'); ends as Osamu goes to Border's upper echelons (147 end / 148 p.1-7). MAL thread: 'ending with the team preparing to present the proposal to higher-ups'. Ends mid-148.

S2E9. Kido meeting and Hyuse's enrollment conditions incl. Chika as engineer (148-149), then strategizing for Round 6 (150). MAL thread: 'higher ups not allowing... Hyuse joining conditions... upcoming rank wars'. START=149 by majority rule (148 p.7-19 is 13 of the episode's ~48 pages); ends mid-150 (p.1-17).

S2E10. Round 6 (Tamakoma-2 vs Oji vs Ikoma): Oji plans to target Osamu's wires (151), match begins (152), cliffhanger with Yuma engaging Oji Squad as Ikoma arrives (153 'Tatsuhito Ikoma' p.1-13). MAL thread: setup, Osamu's wires countered by Oji, Kuga engages the black team at the end. Ends mid-153.

S2E11. Round 6 melee: Kurauchi/Kashio eliminated, Osamu taken by Oji, Chika blasts terrain to escape, Yuma's Grasshopper-debris trip on Oji (157 p.1-10). MAL thread lists these beats (grasshopper debris = ch 157) and the three-way standoff. Ends mid-157.

S2 finale (S2E12). Round 6 ends in Tamakoma-2's win (157-158), Hyuse's one-day rise to B-rank (159 'Hyuse 3'), joins as 4th combatant (160 'Hyuse 4'). ANN review: ends 'once Hyuse gets suited up in his Tamakoma 2 uniform'; MAL poster: 'doesn't adapt the entirety of chapter 160, the rest will be in S3'. Ends mid-160 (p.12-13, 17-19 deferred to ep 86). afg season line 'adapted from manga 120 to 160'.

S3 premiere (S3E1). Finishes ch 160, then Yuri Rindo & Michael Cronin return and Border's founding history is told in Kido's old room (161-162 'Tamakoma Branch 4-5'). MAL S3E1 thread describes exactly these beats; MAL S3E4 poster: 'the adaptation of this season started in chapter 160'. Clean chapter end.

S3E2. Ema at Kageura's family okonomiyaki shop with the rivals (163 'Yuzuru Ema 2'), Osamu/Usami trigger talk and anxiety (164), pre-match prep (165 p.1-11). MAL thread: training, Chika's struggle, okonomiyaki dinner with rivals, loadout decisions. Ends mid-165.

S3E3. Round 7 (Tamakoma-2 vs Azuma vs Kageura vs Suzunari-1) strategy phases (165-166), night-time mall map, Murakami reveals the Black Kogetsu (last page of ch 167); only p.1 of 168 is adapted. MAL thread: strategizing most of the runtime, black Kogetsu, combat begins at the very end. END=168 nominally; reader position is effectively the start of 168.

S3E4. Suzunari-1's fuse-box lights-out tactic (168), Yuma+Hyuse team up (169), Kageura cornered and bails out (170-171). MAL poster (manga reader): 'episode 4 ended at chapter 171' - exact independent pin. START=168 because ep 88 adapted only its first page. Ends mid-171 (p.1-10).

S3E5. Yuma+Hyuse eliminate Murakami (171-172), Osamu bails out after Azuma's ambush (172 end/173), Chika's Meteor guts the mall (173 'Azuma Squad'); ends on the Azuma-vs-Tamakoma endgame setup (173 end: 3 points from No.2). MAL thread lists these beats. Clean chapter end.

S3E6. Round 7 conclusion: Azuma's dummy beacons (174), Hyuse sniped and bails out, Chika's Meteor barrage forces Azuma Squad out, Tamakoma-2 tied 3rd; last page = Ninomiya/Tsuji/Izumi discussing Tamakoma-2 (175 end). MAL thread: round ends, Hyuse eliminated by Azuma, 3rd place, Ninomiya-Izumi discussion. Exact end pinned.

S3E7. 'Hyuse is a Neighbor' rumour and Netsuki's PR plan (176 'Eizo Netsuki'), Osamu's captaincy and Round 8 preview (177 'Osamu Mikumo 17'). MAL thread matches (rumours, memory-erasure talk, Round 8 matchups). Two full chapters.

S3E8. Yakiniku run-in with Ninomiya Squad / Hatohara talk (178 'Ninomiya Squad'), Chika confronts her inability to shoot people after Hyuse's challenge (179 'Chika Amatori 7'). MAL thread: character episode on exactly this. Ends mid-179 (p.20-21 in ep 94).

S3E9. Midorikawa introduces Satomi (180 'Kazuma Satomi'); Yuma spars Obishima, then Yuba's quick-draw humbles him (181 'Takuma Yuba'). MAL thread: 'Kuga schools Yukari... then humiliated by her commander Yuba'. Clean chapter end.

S3E10. Report-back and strength comparisons at Tamakoma Branch (182-183), role shift and first half of the four-squad pre-match planning (184 p.1-9). MAL thread confirms a setup-only episode (final battle 'still one episode away'); no independent pin of the 183/184 seam - hence medium. Ends mid-184.

S3E11. Round 8 (Tamakoma-2 vs Ninomiya vs Yuba vs Ikoma) begins (184 end/185 'Ninomiya Squad 2'), Hyuse isolated against the temporary alliance (186 'Hyuse 8'), cliffhanger at 187 p.1-3. MAL poster gives the continuation point as 'Chapter 187' - exact independent pin. START=185 by majority rule (184 p.9-23 is a 15-page tail).

S3E12. Hyuse's 1-v-6 stand (187-188), Chika's Meteor sniped by Tonooka (188 'Hyuse 9'), Hyuse takes out Ikoma with Viper and bails out (189 'Chika Amatori 8'). MAL thread: exactly these beats. START=187 because ep 96 adapted only p.1-3 of it. Clean chapter end.

S3E13. Free-for-all after Hyuse's exit (190), sniper hunt, Yuma's pinball combo vs Obishima (191-192 'Masataka Ninomiya 3'), Ninomiya vs Yuba resolved on the first page of 193. MAL thread: everyone fighting, sniper trap, Kuga's pinball technique, 'Yuba and Ninomiya short but sweet'. Only p.1 of 193 adapted.

S3 finale (S3E14). Ninomiya's Hornet stalemate (193), final assault (194), Chika's killing shot on Tsuji and Tamakoma-2's win (195), first four pages of the post-match review (196). Sportskeeda: 'adapted chapters 193-196... only four pages of chapter 196'; WDTALO: ends vol 22 ch 196, first few pages. Confirms existing anchor 196. Aired 2022-01-23 after the Tonga-eruption delay.

annotations.note: S1 finale (ep 73) pulled forward ch 121 p.15-19, all of 122, 123 p.1-8/12-13/17-19 and 124 p.1-2/6-18 to close S1; S2 premiere (ep 74, five years later) re-adapts ch 120 p.17-19, 121 p.1-11, 123 p.9-19 and 124 in full before advancing to 125. Ch 122 appears only in ep 73.
S1 finale grafted ch 136 p.12 and 18-19 (post-invasion 'Round 5 begins' beat) twelve chapters ahead of its place; ep 78 later adapts 136 p.12-19 in sequence.
ep 77 shows ch 136 p.1-12 and jumps to the final page 19; ep 78 opens by covering p.12-19 in order.
S2 finale adapts ch 160 p.1-11 and 14-16 (skipping p.12-13, 17-19); S3 premiere re-covers p.12-19, so the 160 seam straddles the season break.
ep 88 adapts only p.1 of ch 168 (the combat kickoff); ep 89 adapts 168 in full - START of ep 89 is 168.
ep 96 ends on ch 187 p.1-3; ep 97 adapts 187 p.3-23 - START of ep 97 is 187.
ep 98 adapts only p.1 of ch 193 (Yuba bails out); ep 99 adapts 193 p.2-17 - START of ep 99 is 193.

repairs.why: stored list is garbled (121 duplicated, 122 omitted, the ch 136 graft omitted). end_chapter 124 and start 121 stand. Adjacent to the target range and needed to explain ep 74's re-adaptation.

structure.notes: Three season entries confirmed and cumulative numbering verified: 20729 = eps 1-73; 114087 (World Trigger 2nd Season, 12 eps, 2021-01-10..2021-04-04) = our 74-85; 127400 (World Trigger 3rd Season, 14 eps, 2021-10-10..2022-01-23) = our 86-99. Wikipedia's episode list numbers S2 as 74-85 and S3 as 86-99; fandom infobox '|Episode = 74 |Number = 1'; worldtriggerwiki '|Total = 85 |Episode = 12' - all identical to our numbering, so the only conversions applied were MAL/ANN per-season thread numbers (S2 ep N = our 73+N; S3 ep N = our 85+N). No OVAs, movies or specials exist for this franchise; no order-only entries. Coverage: S2 = ch 120 (3-page tail) .. 160 (vols 15-18), S3 = ch 160 .. 196 p.4 (vols 18-22); afg's season lines ('120 to 160', '160 to 196') match. S3 was extended from 12 to 14 episodes in Dec 2021; ep 79 aired a week late (2021 Fukushima earthquake coverage) and ep 99 a week late (2022 Tonga eruption coverage) - our air dates already reflect the TV Asahi dates. No filler in S2/S3 (all filler is S1 eps 49-63); all 26 rows correctly typed canon. Title variants seen: afg calls ep 85 'Rookie', ep 91 'Judgment', ep 99 'Resolve'; fandom calls ep 76 'Decisive Battle' - our Crunchyroll titles match Wikipedia.

flags_for_sean: continue_from_chapter: entry says 197, but ep 99 adapts only ch 196 p.1-4 of 23 (fandom page split; Sportskeeda 'only four pages of chapter 196'; WDTALO 'the anime only adapts the first few pages'). Recommend continue point 196 (mangashed's '197' skips the rest of the post-match review). Source: https://www.sportskeeda.com/anime/where-pick-world-trigger-manga-anime-explained , https://wheredoestheanimeleaveoff.com/where-does-the-world-trigger-anime-end-in-the-manga/ , https://worldtrigger.fandom.com/wiki/Resolution

Source independence: animefillerguide's 26 per-episode lists are identical to the fandom wiki's (including the odd '120,121,123,124,125' list for ep 74), and worldtriggerwiki.com is the same community post-fandom migration - treat the three as one lineage. Independent pins used instead: MAL manga-reader posts (ep 74 exact chapters; ep 85 '160 not fully adapted'; ep 86 'season started in ch 160'; ep 89 'ended at ch 171'; ep 96 'continue at ch 187'), CBR (S2 starts ch 121), ANN S2E12 review, Sportskeeda/WDTALO (ep 99), and chapter-final events matched against fandom chapter summaries elsewhere. Eps 75 and 95 have no end-pinning independent check and are marked medium.

START convention applied (Sean's majority rule): opening tails smaller than the bulk of the episode -> START = next full chapter (eps 76, 78, 79, 82, 83, 84, 85, 86, 88, 90, 94, 96). Exceptions noted in-line: ep 74 START=121 (p.1-11 is the chapter head; its remainder was already adapted in S1), eps 89/97/99 START = the chapter whose previous-episode share was 1-3 pages. Page splits are all preserved in chapters_adapted if you prefer a different convention.

Low priority, outside range: ep 72's stored end 121 rests on ch 121 p.1-2 and 12-15 only (bulk is 119-120 p.1-16); the honest resume point after ep 72 is ch 120 p.17. Consider a continue point of 120 for ep 72 if S1's tail is ever re-passed.
